worlds.name: Goblin World
worlds.theme: Memory, accelerated history, industry, abandonment, and myth.
worlds.centralQuestion: Did the goblins remember Kael as savior, god, liar, or myth?
worlds.tone: Restless, inventive, wounded, argumentative, brilliant, spiritually divided.
worlds.timeLaw: 1 Second Dimension day equals 1 Goblin World month.
worlds.conflict: Goblin civilization cannot agree whether Kael represents hope, abandonment, false divinity, or a test of self-rule.

worlds.name: Orc World
worlds.theme: Strength, honor, childhood, protection, and the inheritance of war.
worlds.centralQuestion: Can a race built on war redefine strength?
worlds.tone: Proud, austere, loud in ritual, gentle in private, ashamed of inherited cruelty.
worlds.timeLaw: Unconfirmed; no invented time distortion may be treated as canon.
worlds.conflict: Traditionalists believe strength must dominate; reformers believe strength means children need not become weapons.

worlds.name: Beastkin Territories
worlds.theme: Freedom versus civilization, nature versus walls, instinct versus law.
worlds.centralQuestion: Does civilization protect nature or destroy it?
worlds.tone: Lush, dangerous, beautiful, territorial, ceremonial, emotionally direct.
worlds.timeLaw: Unconfirmed; seasonal anomalies remain mystery rather than settled law.
villains: Huntress Mara of the Blood Moon
worlds.conflict: Some see city law as protection from famine and slavery; others see walls as the slow death of the wild soul.

worlds.name: Demon Realms
worlds.theme: Fear, beauty, forbidden knowledge, law, and trust.
worlds.centralQuestion: Can those feared as monsters ever be trusted?
worlds.tone: Elegant, dangerous, theatrical, scholarly, romantic, cruel in old law, hungry for redemption.
worlds.timeLaw: Contract and school calendars exist; deeper temporal irregularities remain unconfirmed.
heroes: Professor Sareth of the Mercy Index
villains: Duke Varos of the Living Signature
worlds.conflict: Demon civilization contains art, law, schools, family, and love, but its history of contracts and fear makes trust explosive.

worlds.name: Dark Elf Territories
worlds.theme: Truth versus stability, memory versus safety, shadow versus silence.
worlds.centralQuestion: Is a painful truth better than a peaceful lie?
worlds.tone: Quiet, elegant, suspicious, poetic, wounded, precise, morally dangerous.
worlds.timeLaw: Archive eras are named for truths sealed, revealed, or destructive; no universal ratio is established.
worlds.conflict: Dark Elf society survived by controlling information; opening truth may heal history or destroy fragile peace.

worlds.name: Bunny Trade Nations
worlds.theme: Commerce, connection, debt, logistics, and the moral weight of price.
worlds.tone: Bright, fast-talking, charming, wealthy, anxious, practical, playful, sharp.
worlds.timeLaw: Trade clocks vary by contract route and delivery window; no single universal ratio.
heroes: Lord Pollen of the Open Road
worlds.conflict: Trade delivers medicine and connection, but the same systems can turn survival into debt.

worlds.name: Dog Tribe Frontiers
worlds.theme: Duty, loyalty, borders, oaths, and moral fracture.
worlds.centralQuestion: What happens when loyalty and morality disagree?
worlds.tone: Warm, direct, loyal, frontier-practical, ceremonial, protective, quietly haunted.
worlds.timeLaw: Patrol cycles, lost companions, and oath renewals shape calendars; no universal ratio.
worlds.conflict: Loyalty is sacred, but a sacred oath becomes terrifying when leaders order harm in the name of protection.
